mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% consistently predicts positive 20-day S&P 500 returns due to compressed discount rates and accommodative monetary policy, as evidenced by historical data where low FEDFUNDS periods correlate with equity market gains.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS below 0.5% and 20-day returns negative in more than 40% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.5%, it signals economic weakness and potential recession, leading to negative 5-day S&P 500 returns as investors flee risk.
failure_condition: UNRATE above 5.5% and 5-day returns positive in more than 40% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising inflation (CPIAUCSL > 0.5% monthly growth) and stagnant monetary policy (FEDFUNDS < 0.25%) signals the Federal Reserve is behind the curve, causing negative 60-day S&P 500 returns as investors anticipate aggressive rate hikes.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL rises >0.5% and FEDFUNDS < 0.25%, 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (defined by GDP growth > 2% and unemployment < 4.5%), high housing starts (HOUST > 1500) indicate overbuilding and potential market correction, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns as investors anticipate economic slowdown.
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime, when HOUST > 1500, 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds 108.0, it indicates strong economic activity and growth, leading to positive 60-day S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: INDPRO above 108.0 and 60-day returns negative in more than 40% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL > 0.5% monthly growth) and federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 0.25%) signals aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative 5-day S&P 500 returns as investors react to policy shifts.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL rises >0.5% and FEDFUNDS > 0.25%, 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4.0%, it indicates a tight labor market and potential wage inflation, leading to positive 60-day S&P 500 returns as investors anticipate strong economic growth and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: UNRATE below 4.0% and 60-day returns negative in more than 40% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS > 0.25% and CPIAUCSL > 260), high housing starts (HOUST > 1500) signal overvaluation in the housing market, leading to negative 5-day S&P 500 returns as investors anticipate policy-driven market corrections.
failure_condition: In the monetary tightening cycle regime, when HOUST > 1500, 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.
